summary: Dermot Killingley is an indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1953–1957) and SOAS. He served at the University of Malaya (~1967–1970) and Newcastle University (~1970–2000), becoming Reader in Religious Studies.

Dermott Joseph Walsh works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a BA from Trinity College Dublin in 2003, an MA from Leiden University in 2009, and a PhD from UCLA in 2018 under William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramkrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910) and Superintendent for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917).
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied with Gaton Ngawang Legpa, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ngawang Nyima, and participated in a University of Washington research project from 1960 to 1972.

Dhammanandā is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) under Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe. She also studied under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama.

Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Dhammasakkaro and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) under K. L. Dhammajoti. He later served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1924). He held posts at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma (1932–2022) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under David Friedman and the traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He has held posts at the Open University as associate lecturer (attested 2017) and at the University of Chester (2019).

Di Luo specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed a master's under James Steele and earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016) under Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge.

Diana L. Eck is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College (~1963–1967), SOAS (~1967–1968), and Harvard University (~1968–1976). She joined the faculty at Harvard University as a professor around 1976.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1977. In 2005, she was attested as an Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane E. Riggs completed her PhD at UCLA in 2010 under William M. Bodiford and studied under Myōsei Tatsuguchi. She has held posts at Kenyon College (2010), Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University (2017).
Diane L. Howard is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed graduate studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
Dickwela Piyananda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the Catholic University of America under the supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at École Polytechnique under the doctoral supervision of Francisco Varela.

Diego Loukota is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2019.
Dieter George (1935–1985) was an Indologist who held a post at the Berlin State Library from circa 1967 to 1985, succeeding Wolfgang Voigt by 1985.

Dieter Schlingloff is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He held posts at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (1953–1959), University of Kiel (1967–1972), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (Professor 1972–1996; Honorary Professor from 1996).
